text.p: Leading Belgian banks Kredietbank (KB) and Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) were smarting on Monday from waning merger speculation, dealers said.
KB was down 1.8 percent at 14,300 francs, after earlier touching 14,200, and BBL 1.4 percent at 9,420 francs.
KB started weakening on Wednesday after the bank quashed merger speculation by re-affirming in a newspaper interview that it would prefer to remain independent.
KB said last month it was in "exploratory" talks with Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank and Belgium's CERA Bank.
Also last Wednesday, KB was hit by a downgrade to "neutral" from "accumulate" by brokerage Merrill Lynch.

BBL started slipping last Friday after chief executive officer Michel Tilmant said in a magazine interview that the so-called Great Belgian bank project -- a merger with Belgium's biggest bank Generale Bank -- had been put "in the freezer". Generale Bank itself was down 0.3 percent at 14,300.
But one dealer said on Monday that if any major news had to be expected, it was more likely to come from BBL than from KB.
